A small release: a global hotkey for New chat, New chat getting a tmux window of its own, and WSL sessions on Windows getting their orbs back.

## New

- **Ctrl+Alt+N opens New chat from anywhere.** If New chat is already open, the hotkey brings it to the front instead of opening a second one. To use a different chord, set `newChatHotkey` in settings.json, the same way `toggleOrbsHotkey` works.

## Changed

- **New chat now opens in a tmux window of its own** in your tmux session. It used to split the window you were working in.

## Fixed

- **WSL sessions on Windows now get orbs.** A Claude Code session running inside WSL never drew an orb, while the same session started from a Windows prompt did. This is fixed by updating the app. The hooks don't need reinstalling.
- **A missing folder, or one with `#{` in its name, no longer starts Claude in your home folder under tmux.** This applies to New chat and to attaching from an orb. tmux quietly fell back to `$HOME`; the command now fails instead of running in the wrong place.
- **An invalid hotkey override no longer binds a key you can't press.** Values such as `Ctrl+Alt+5`, `F5` or `Ctrl+999` used to be accepted and bind a key nobody could press, or no key at all. Both hotkeys now fall back to their default. Only A–Z and 0–9 are accepted as the key.
- **A hotkey the OS refuses is now logged** to `hotkeys.log`, next to `crash.log`, so a chord another app already holds shows up somewhere instead of failing silently.
- **Choosing New chat… from the tray when it's already open now brings it in front of other apps.** Before, it only moved to the front of Claude Buddy's own windows.

## Known limitations

No real key press was tested on either platform, because nothing in the test suite presses keys. Ctrl+Alt+N is covered by headless UI tests but has not been checked by hand on macOS or Windows.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.7-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.7-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.7-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

## Upgrading

Replace the app as usual. **On macOS, if you re-install you have to re-grant the Automation and Local Network permissions.** Replacing `/Applications/Claude Buddy.app` gives the app a new code identity, and macOS doesn't carry those permissions over to it. Without Automation, click-to-focus stops working; without Local Network, anything on your LAN, such as an OpenClaw gateway, can't be reached. Re-grant both in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
